A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MolParser and contain readable main text, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections 8–13. Their shared content and revised material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original OCSR benchmark results, training and augmentation ablations, molecular property prediction experiments, and qualitative evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and reports revised OCSR comparisons, additional ablation results, and new dataset analyses and failure examples.

M1.justification: The Swin encoder, MLP connector, BART decoder, next-token objective, curriculum pretraining, real-data fine-tuning, and active-learning procedure remain unchanged. E-SMILES is a renamed representation with the same encoding rules; the new data-engine diagram supplies documentation rather than establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Section 6.1 and Table 2 add the 200-image ColoredBG evaluation and remove the dedicated large-molecule USPTO-10K-L benchmark. This adjusts test-scenario coverage within OCSR. The training corpus, ordinary and Markush WildMol subsets, other retained benchmarks, and five molecular property prediction tasks remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes Image2Graph and CEDe and updates DECIMER 2.0 to 2.7. The retained WildMol-10K comparison expands beyond MolGrapher to include OSRA, MolVec, Imago, Img2Mol, DECIMER, and MolScribe. Table 3 likewise adds speed comparisons against Img2Mol, DECIMER, and MolScribe, substantially broadening the practical comparator set.

E3.justification: Table 3 replaces Tanimoto similarity with accuracy and drops the 403-image validation column. Tables 4–5 replace classical-benchmark and validation evaluations with WildMol-10K evaluations. Table 4 adds a pooled-training control, and Table 2 separately evaluates Tiny, Small, and Base variants. These substantially revise the reported evaluation design without establishing changes to the core training recipe.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds a control training on the combined pretraining and fine-tuning data without a separate fine-tuning stage, testing the value of staging. New appendix Figures 5 and 11 add corpus-provenance analysis and representation failure examples. The existing scaling and augmentation questions and earlier qualitative cases remain, although the ablation evaluation coverage changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report average molecular property prediction ROC-AUC scores after five runs in Table 6. Neither adds experimental confidence intervals, significance tests, seed specifications, or other uncertainty reporting. The active-learning five-fold procedure is also unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2's v1 MolParser row reports USPTO/UoB accuracy of 98.8/97.6, whereas v2's Base row reports 93.0/91.8; the cause is unexplained. Numerous comparator values and result entries also change. Table 3 replaces Base's Markush Tanimoto similarity of 0.774 with accuracy of 38.1%, which is not a comparable performance decrease. New ColoredBG and ablation results are added; Table 6's property prediction results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The representation and index definitions in Section 9 remain unchanged, and neither version contains formal theorems or proofs. Figure 4 corrects an illustrative abstract-ring index from 9 to 0 without changing the underlying definition.

C1.justification: The three central contributions—extended SMILES, MolParser-7M, and the MolParser model—remain. The introduction withdraws the specific claim of state-of-the-art USPTO accuracy exceeding 98% and centers its performance claim on WildMol accuracy. Speed and industrial applicability receive greater emphasis, while the overall contribution scope remains stable.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 newly identifies limited size, systematic biases, and annotation noise in classical benchmarks. Section 12 and Figure 11 add explicit E-SMILES limitations involving dashed abstract rings, coordination bonds, special-symbol Markush structures, and long-segment replication. Earlier overlap and charged-molecule failures and the principal mechanism interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Figure 7 newly documents 10% random expert inspection, and Table 3 explicitly includes preprocessing and postprocessing in timing. Section 11 revises the reported training hardware from eight RTX 4090 cards to eight RTX 4090D GPUs. The introduction's 300k-to-400k correction agrees with the existing Table 1 count. Training hyperparameters and embedded dataset/demo links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work expands to cover InChI output, Image2InChI, and MMSSC-Net, and the ColoredBG source is newly cited. CEDe and the ResNet reference disappear. These are limited updates within the retained positioning around image-captioning versus graph-based OCSR and extended SMILES versus earlier representations.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section sequence remain intact. Local rewrites affect the introduction's performance summary, related work, evaluation discussion, and limitations. Terminology is standardized around E-SMILES and WildMol, and the author list changes. This is selective editing rather than a broad narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Tables 2–5 are substantially restructured, and Table 6 moves from a compact column-width display to a larger full-width table. The appendix adds provenance charts, a data-engine diagram, representation failure panels, and a speed–accuracy plot. Dataset-distribution plots are redrawn, the dataset-size bubble panel is removed, and retained augmentation and qualitative figures are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the central real-world evaluation more informative through broader WildMol comparisons, Markush accuracy reporting, and the pooled-training control in Table 4. Concrete representation limitations and corpus-provenance information also improve transparency. These gains are tempered by removal of USPTO-10K-L and multi-benchmark ablation evidence, plus unexplained revisions to classical-benchmark scores. The net benefit is a limited improvement in evidential clarity and qualification.
